course_title: Applied Research in Criminology and Criminal Justice 2
course_description:
Research and project planning skills are highly valued by employers and are widely used in academic, government and non-governmental agencies, private companies and community organisations. This course aims continues to enhance the skills and knowledge of theory and research methods developed in other degree courses through the completion of an applied year-long group research project in the field of crime and justice. Students will develop their research skills in response to current issues and build confidence in delivering impactful outputs that are valued by industry.

This course is only available to BCCJ students and continues on project and team work from CRIM3201. Students become skilled in project planning, team work, and industry liaison.

This course should be completed in the final year of study. Students must complete CRIM3202 in the semester immediately after CRIM3201.

Welcome to CRIM3202. I trust that you will enjoy this course, building upon the foundation established in the previous semester. This continuation will be among the most exciting, relevant, and challenging learning experiences in your degree. As a ‘capstone’ experience, it provides opportunities to apply and advance the research skills and knowledge developed in earlier criminology courses and polish your employability portfolio preparing you for your professional future. You will continue to work on your 'real world' applied research project with your industry partner from the government, community, or corporate sector. The focus remains on developing critical research evaluation skills including team collaboration and project planning, data collection, analysis, report writing and dissemination to diverse audiences.

assessment_details.task_description: The Methods Defence Assessment is an opportunity for you to individually demonstrate your understanding of research methods and respective analytic approaches to your current research project. This task aims to strengthen capability to effectively engage with both qualitative and quantitative research methods by the conclusion of the course. In this in-person individual practical, you will demonstrate critical understanding of your methodological choices through structured questioning that explores rationale, implementation, analysis, and limitations. The assessment also requires you to articulate complex methodological concepts and justify decisions against alternatives while acknowledging methodological constraints. Marking criteria: Criteria including rubrics are available in the ‘Assessments’ folder on the course Blackboard site. AI Use: This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. A single sided page of notes (A4) can be used during this assignment to sparingly prompt/reference specific elements or evidence. Successful completion of this assessment will require you to (independent of notes) understand your research methods and critically engage in a discussion about your project aims, methodological approach (including limitations, benefits and feasibility) and an exploration of alternative methods. A failure to reference AI use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct Policy. Additional resources are available through UQ AI Student Hub . assessment_details.task_description: Final Report The Final Project Report is the main product of the research team’s efforts over the course of the year. The Final Report is an opportunity for your team to demonstrate your research evaluation skills and knowledge acquired through your applied industry research project. The Final Report should be well structured and written to a high standard. The Final Report (6000-7000 words) will include an introduction to the research problem, aims and questions, literature, key concepts or theoretical framework, methodology, results, discussion and conclusion (with implications). All literature, sources and data must be authentic, verifiable, appropriately evidenced and accurately referenced including use of AI tools. Further task details and requirements (including relevant marking criteria) can be found in the relevant Assessment folder on Blackboard. AI Use: This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which AI may provide limited support and guidance. A failure to reference AI use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct Policy. Students may be required to complete an AI usage declaration and submit it with their assessment. Additional resources are available through UQ AI Student Hub . Project Progress Tasks Each team member is required to complete a weekly Project Progress Task (weeks 1-12, excluding 4,8,13) to document their specific contributions, commitment to deliverables for the following week, and to assess group progress. The Project Progress Tasks are to be completed via a Qualtrics survey link in class or MS Teams as relevant for the specific week. Your contribution to the Project Progress Tasks will be assessed by the course coordinator during your in-class project work and through the contributions you make on MS Teams during weeks 1-12 (excluding assessment weeks). Each project progress task is worth .5 points for a total of 5 points towards your individual report mark. Grading Impact : Individual final marks will be calculated as: Group Project Mark (max 30 points) + .5 x each completed project progress task x 10 (= max 5 points) x PAF (via Buddycheck) = Individual Mark (max 35 points). Buddycheck: This assessment includes a Buddycheck. Each team member will complete a Buddycheck form by the due date which will provide an opportunity to reflect on the contribution each member of the team has made to the WHOLE group project. The Buddycheck form may be used to adjust marks according to contribution. Read full task description Hide full task description
